title: LLM Preference Alignment Pipeline with Bradley-Terry Reward Modeling & Direct Preference Optimization
problem: Supervised fine-tuning teaches language models task formats but fails to align generation tone, safety boundaries, and nuanced human preferences. Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) using traditional PPO is notoriously unstable, suffering from hyperparameter sensitivity, value network divergence, and reward hacking. This project builds a direct preference alignment pipeline in Python and PyTorch using the TRL library. The system trains a Bradley-Terry pairwise reward model on human preference datasets, optimizes model policies using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) with implicit reward formulations and KL divergence penalties, prevents catastrophic forgetting, and evaluates alignment win rates against baseline supervised models.

use_cases.title: Conversational Safety & Hate Speech Refusal Alignment
use_cases.first_sentence: Consumer AI application developers need conversational assistants that politely refuse harmful instructions while remaining helpful on benign queries.
use_cases.second_sentence: The alignment pipeline trains a reward model on safety preference pairs, optimizing model weights via DPO to eliminate toxic outputs without over-refusal.

use_cases.title: Executive Summary Conciseness and Tone Calibration
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise business intelligence tools require summarization models that consistently produce concise, bulleted executive briefings rather than verbose narrative text.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system aligns an open-source model against executive preference pairs, ensuring generated summaries strictly prioritize key quantitative takeaways.

use_cases.title: Code Review Tone & Constructive Feedback Alignment
use_cases.first_sentence: Engineering organizations deploying automated code review bots need comments that provide constructive architectural suggestions rather than dismissive remarks.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine trains on paired senior engineer feedback demonstrations, aligning review bots to suggest specific refactoring diffs with polite explanatory notes.

hard_parts: Training a robust Bradley-Terry reward model that scores preference margins accurately without overfitting to response length bias
Deriving and optimizing the closed-form DPO objective without requiring unstable actor-critic reinforcement learning loops
Calibrating the KL divergence reference model constraint beta parameter to prevent policy collapse into degenerate repetitive strings
Evaluating win rates using automated LLM-as-a-judge protocols with position-bias counterbalancing
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating preference dataset loaders, reward model training scripts, and DPO trainers
Comprehensive training curves in Weights & Biases showing margin growth, policy reward increase, and KL divergence stabilization
Anti-fake verification script presenting an unseen paired preference test and verifying reward model assigns correct higher score to preferred text

components.name: Preference Pair Ingestion & Length-Normalization Pipeline
components.purpose: Loads chosen-rejected response pairs, normalizes response lengths, and constructs tokenized tensors

components.name: Bradley-Terry Pairwise Reward Model Trainer
components.purpose: Trains a scalar reward head on top of transformer backbone using binary cross-entropy preference loss

components.name: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) Trainer
components.purpose: Optimizes policy weights directly from preference pairs with reference model KL divergence regularization

components.name: Reward Score Distribution & Margin Evaluator
components.purpose: Computes reward score histograms and validates margin separation between chosen and rejected candidates

components.name: Win-Rate & Catastrophic Forgetting Benchmark Suite
components.purpose: Measures pairwise win-rate against SFT baseline and asserts retention of core knowledge benchmarks

components.name: Alignment Experiment Telemetry & Runbook Documentation
components.purpose: Documents hyperparameter configurations, beta sweep findings, and preference data curation guides

architecture.data_flow: Chosen and rejected prompt-response pairs enter the ingestion pipeline; text sequences tokenize and pad with uniform formatting; the reward model trains to predict higher scalar values for chosen completions; the DPO training loop loads the base SFT model alongside frozen reference weights; DPO updates LoRA policy parameters by maximizing the log-likelihood of chosen completions relative to rejected completions penalizing KL divergence; evaluation harnesses score aligned outputs against held-out preference prompts; telemetry logs to Weights & Biases.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: KL penalty coefficient (beta=0.1) preventing policy drift from reference model; gradient norm clipping at 1.0.

targets.method: Percentage of held-out preference test pairs where the reward model scores the chosen response higher than the rejected response
targets.input: 500 held-out pairwise preference test samples spanning helpfulness, conciseness, and safety domains
targets.environment: Standard GPU instance (12GB+ VRAM) or CPU evaluation harness
targets.minimum_pass: Reward classification accuracy is >= 72.0% across 500 test pairs
targets.target: Reward classification accuracy is >= 81.5% across 500 test pairs
targets.report: Reward model accuracy and margin distribution evaluation report

targets.metric: DPO Aligned Policy Win-Rate Over SFT Baseline
targets.method: Pairwise win-rate evaluated across 200 held-out evaluation prompts judged by automated evaluator with position swapping
targets.input: 200 test prompts evaluated for response helpfulness, safety, and conciseness
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU with PyTorch inference runtime
targets.minimum_pass: Aligned model achieves >= 65.0% win-rate over unaligned SFT baseline across 200 prompts
targets.target: Aligned model achieves >= 78.0% win-rate over unaligned SFT baseline across 200 prompts
targets.report: Pairwise alignment win-rate evaluation summary table

targets.method: Average per-token KL divergence between aligned policy and frozen SFT reference model across training epochs
targets.input: Training trajectory across 1,000 DPO optimization steps with beta=0.1
targets.environment: PyTorch training loop with CUDA execution
targets.minimum_pass: Average per-token KL divergence is < 0.15 across training epochs
targets.target: Average per-token KL divergence is < 0.08 across training epochs
targets.report: Training KL divergence trajectory and policy stability log

riskiest_component.name: Policy Degeneration and Repetitive Output Collapse During DPO
riskiest_component.mitigation: Tune beta coefficient between 0.05 and 0.2 and evaluate token diversity metrics during training.
riskiest_component.fallback: Increase beta to 0.25 to tightly anchor policy to reference model.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an LLM preference alignment pipeline in Python/PyTorch using Bradley-Terry reward modeling and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
worksheet.q2: Target users: AI alignment engineers, safety researchers, and enterprise LLM developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: conversational safety refusal alignment, executive summary tone calibration, and constructive code review feedback.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: Bradley-Terry reward modeling without length bias, DPO closed-form optimization, KL divergence penalty calibration, and position-bias counterbalancing in win-rate evals.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 3,000 preference pairs in JSONL format, DPO configuration YAMLs, and 200 evaluation prompts. Public preference data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 16GB RAM, free Colab/Kaggle GPU, $0 cost, zero paid cloud services. Fallback: CPU training with Qwen-0.5B.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: policy degeneration during DPO. Fallback: beta hyperparameter sweeps and token diversity monitoring.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: pre-canned reward scores. Anti-fake check 5 scores dynamic unseen safety prompt and asserts reward margin > 1.5 logits.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; public open-source preference datasets only, zero private or sensitive user personal data.
